State expiry helps with this a bit, and account based systems (rather than UTXO) make this particular problem less problematic in the normal case. <@456226577798135808> > The user does not set a max basefee, they set a fee cap (which is base fee + priority fee) if they set it too low (stuck tx), they might want to increase it to make the tx go through but its possible to set max basefee and priority fee independently no? No, you set a maxFeePerGas and a maxPriorityFeePerGas. The former is the max on the sum of the base fee and the priority fee. And that one in turn cannot be higher than maxPriorityFeePerGas. I'm not doing a good job explaining lol, examples work better I think hm i think i understand Say you set a fee cap of 200 Gwei, and a priority fee cap of 100 Gwei. If the base fee for a certain block is 150 Gwei, then you end up paying 200 Gwei (your cap). You pay (=burned) 150 Gwei for the base fee, and 50 Gwei goes to the miner. If you want "traditional style" transactions, you set the fee cap equal to the priority fee cap (or you can even set the latter higher if you want). Then you _always_ end up paying the fee cap, just like you would now always pay the entire gas fee if your tx goes through. For many users that only care about inclusion (and not position), the maxPriorityFeePerGas will be set to 1 Gwei by the wallet (and hidden from the user). The wallet will also set the fee cap to something like 2 x the current base fee (and also hide this from the user by default) So if the base fee is 150 Gwei (like before), a typical tx could have a fee cap of 300 Gwei and a priority fee cap of 1 Gwei. If the base fee stays the same, you end up paying 151 Gwei (150 of which is burned, 1 goes to miner) per unit of gas.
